q: Which category is number one in the OWASP Top 10:2025?
explain: A01:2025 is Broken Access Control, as in 2021. Security Misconfiguration is now second, and Injection dropped to fifth.

q: Which two categories are NEW in the OWASP Top 10:2025? (multiple answers)
explain: The new ones are A03 Software Supply Chain Failures and A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions. SSRF was merged into A01, and Insecure Design has existed since 2021.

q: Where is SSRF in the OWASP Top 10:2025?
options: It is still a separate category, A10
It was merged into A01 Broken Access Control
It was dropped because it's no longer relevant
It was merged into A05 Injection
explain: In the 2025 edition SSRF is part of A01. In the API Security Top 10 (2023) it is still a separate item, API7.

q: What is the correct defense against SQL injection?
options: A WAF in front of the application
explain: Parameterization separates code from data at the database driver level. Filtering and WAFs are additional layers and can be bypassed.

q: GET /api/invoices/1043 returns another user's invoice when you change the number. What is this vulnerability called in the API Top 10?
explain: BOLA (IDOR in the web context): the API doesn't check whether the object belongs to the user requesting it.

q: A user sends PATCH /api/users/me with {"role":"admin"} and becomes an admin. Which API Top 10 category?
options: API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (mass assignment)
explain: The API accepts a field the user isn't allowed to change. Defense: an explicit allowlist of fields (DTO), not binding the entire JSON to the model.

q: How should user passwords be stored?
options: A slow, salted hash: Argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt
explain: Passwords aren't encrypted, because anything encrypted can be decrypted. A fast hash (SHA-256) allows billions of guesses per second on a GPU. Argon2id/bcrypt are deliberately slow and use a salt.

q: The is_admin() function returns True when the authorization service doesn't respond. Which OWASP Top 10:2025 category?
options: A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (fail open)
explain: A system that grants access on error fails open. The correct behavior is fail closed: an error means denial.

q: Someone publishes the internal package 'firma-utils' on the public npm registry with a higher version, and the build pulls it in. What is this attack called and which category does it belong to?
options: Dependency confusion, A03 Software Supply Chain Failures
explain: Dependency confusion exploits the fact that the package manager prefers the public registry or a higher version. Defense: scoped packages, a private registry as the only source, lock files.

q: Which type of vulnerability is HARDEST for automated scanners (SAST, DAST) to find?
explain: A scanner doesn't know which object belongs to which user or what is correct from a business standpoint. That requires authorization tests, code review and threat modeling.

q: What is the main purpose of the Content-Security-Policy header?
options: It restricts where a page may load and execute scripts from, mitigating XSS
explain: CSP is a second layer of defense against XSS: even if an attacker injects a script, the browser won't execute it if the source isn't allowed. HSTS enforces HTTPS.

q: Click the lines where user input becomes part of code (A05 Injection).
explain: Line 10 puts the customer parameter straight into SQL with an f-string: ' OR '1'='1 returns all orders. Fix: a parameterized query, db.execute("... WHERE customer = ?", (name,)). Line 16 passes host to a shell (shell=True), so 127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd runs a second command. Fix: subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host]) without a shell, plus validating that host is an IP or a hostname.
